claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT can be used to determine whether a system has a ferromagnetic ground state.
The determination can be made by comparing the total energies of magnetic and non-magnetic configurations.
The modeled initial state is spin-unpolarized and non-magnetic.
Ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and non-magnetic configurations should be tested to identify the lowest-total-energy state.
The proposed calculations represent the 0 K ground state.
GGA is an appropriate example of an exchange-correlation functional for these calculations.
The supercell must adequately represent chemical disorder and lattice-structure effects.
Local electronic structure and induced transition-metal magnetic moments mediate magnetic exchange interactions.
A ferromagnetic configuration with lower total energy than the non-magnetic and competing magnetic configurations indicates preferential stabilization of a ferromagnetic ground state.
Spin-polarized DFT will predict the ferromagnetic configuration to have lower energy than the non-magnetic and other competing magnetic configurations.
Non-spin-polarized DFT does not account for magnetic ordering.
The inferred ground state may depend on the exchange-correlation functional and the representation of chemical disorder.
A 0 K ground-state calculation does not capture finite-temperature effects and magnetic excitations.
Calculated energy differences and local magnetic moments are sensitive to computational parameters and approximations.
Experimental validation may be necessary to confirm the computational prediction.
A lower energy for a non-magnetic or alternative magnetic configuration than for the ferromagnetic configuration falsifies the proposed ferromagnetic ground state.
Negligible computed magnetic moments would falsify the proposed ferromagnetic ground state.
